Let people pay into your Arc app from any wallet or exchange.

On Arc, pressing Send in a wallet can't reach a savings vault, an escrow or a checkout contract. Doorstep gives each payer an address. The USDC that arrives there is deposited into your contract for the right person within seconds, or sent back.

A wallet's Send button can't reach your contract.

On Arc, USDC is the native coin. Wallets and exchanges send it as a plain transfer. Vaults, escrows and checkouts only accept money through their own deposit function, so a plain transfer to them fails.

Without Doorstep

Wallet or exchangesends toYour vaultReverted

This happened on Arc mainnet on 2 October 2026: a wallet payment into an onramp's escrow failed, and the team had to fund it from a backend script (issue #48).

With Doorstep

Wallet or exchangesends toDoorstep addressdelivered intoYour vaultCredited

Your contract doesn't change. Payers don't connect anything. They send USDC on Arc to an address, as they already know how to.

How a payment gets in.

  1. You create an address

    It's calculated from its instructions: which contract, who gets credited, where refunds go, and until when. Nothing is deployed, and anyone can recompute it to check.

  2. They pay from anywhere

    A wallet's Send button, an exchange withdrawal or an ERC-20 transfer. On Arc these all land in the same USDC balance.

  3. It's delivered automatically

    A delivery bot calls your contract's deposit function within seconds. Its network fee, usually under $0.01, comes out of the payment.

  4. Or it goes back

    If your contract refuses it, or it arrives after the deadline, it's returned to the refund wallet. That wallet can also cancel at any time.

A few lines, or one HTTPS call.

Use the JavaScript SDK in your app, or the hosted API from any backend. Both give you the address, a ready pay page and the payment's status.

No custody. Doorstep never holds funds between transactions. The money can only go to your contract or back to the refund wallet.

Works with your contract as it is. Anything with deposit(uint256 amount, address to) that pulls with transferFrom, which includes every ERC-4626 vault. Other functions work too.

Know when it lands. Signed webhooks for delivered and returned payments, retried for two hours.

API reference SDK guide 
import { createDoorstep } from 'doorstep-arc';

const ds = createDoorstep();            // Arc mainnet

const invoice = ds.depositIntent({
  into: '0xYourVault',                // deposit(amount, to)
  beneficiary: customer,              // who gets credited
  refundTo: customer,                 // if it can't be delivered
  minimum: '25',
  expires: '7d',
  reference: 'inv-1042',
});

ds.depositAddress(invoice);           // show it, or a QR code
ds.toLink(invoice, { amount: '25' });  // a ready pay page
ds.watch(invoice, (e) => {            // waiting, landed, bounced
  if (e.type === 'landed') markPaid('inv-1042');
});
curl -X POST https://api.104-251-218-80.sslip.io/v1/addresses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOORSTEP_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "into": "0xYourVault",
    "beneficiary": "0xCustomer",
    "refundTo": "0xCustomer",
    "amount": "25",
    "reference": "inv-1042",
    "webhookUrl": "https://yourapp.com/hooks/doorstep"
  }'

# 201 Created
{
  "address": "0x6d97…0d58",
  "payLink": "https://…/app/#i=…",
  "registered": true,
  "invoice": { "state": "unpaid", "remaining": "25" }
}
// POST to your webhookUrl when a payment lands
import crypto from 'node:crypto';

app.post('/hooks/doorstep', express.raw({ type: '*/*' }), (req, res) => {
  const ts = req.get('x-doorstep-timestamp');
  const expected = 'v1=' + crypto
    .createHmac('sha256', process.env.DOORSTEP_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
    .update(`${ts}.${req.body}`).digest('hex');
  if (req.get('x-doorstep-signature') !== expected) return res.sendStatus(401);

  const event = JSON.parse(req.body);
  // { type: 'payment.delivered', data: { reference: 'inv-1042', amount: '24.996', txUrl } }
  if (event.type === 'payment.delivered') markPaid(event.data.reference);
  res.sendStatus(200);
});

Everything a payment needs, end to end.

JavaScript SDK
Build addresses offline, describe them to payers in plain words, watch their status, deliver or cancel.
Hosted API
One HTTPS call returns an address and a pay page, registered for automatic delivery. API keys and rate limits included.
Webhooks
A signed notice when a payment is delivered or returned, with retries for two hours.
Invoices
Ask for an exact amount. Part payments are tracked, and nothing is delivered until all of it is there.
Pay pages
A QR code, live status and a Deliver button anyone can press, at a link you can send to anyone.
Delivery bot
Public and always on, repaid from each payment. It only delivers what repays its gas, and anyone can run another.

Built on what makes Arc different.

Gas is paid in USDCThe delivery bot is repaid in the same coin it spent, by simple arithmetic. No price oracle, no swaps, no float to manage.
One balance, two interfacesNative sends and ERC-20 transfers both arrive in the same balance, so a single sweep handles both.
Native USDC moves with SELFDESTRUCTAn 8-byte contract created and destroyed in one transaction is the entire sweep. The address is empty again afterwards and can be paid again, even by exchanges that send with a fixed gas limit.
Fast finality, fees under a centCredit is final as soon as the delivery is included, and small payments are still worth delivering.

Where the money can go, and where it can't.

Only two destinations

A payment can only be delivered into the contract in its instructions, or returned to its refund wallet. Not to Doorstep, not to the delivery bot, not to anyone else.

Nothing can be redirected

The address is calculated from the instructions. Change one word and you get a different address, so a handed-out address always does what it says.

The payer is protected

Payments that can't be delivered, or arrive after the deadline, go back automatically. The refund wallet can also take them back early.

Not audited yet

Doorstep is new and hasn't had a security audit. The code and tests are public. Use small amounts until it has been reviewed.

Questions people ask.

Which wallets and exchanges work?

Anything that can send USDC on the Arc network: browser and mobile wallets, and exchange withdrawals that support Arc. The payer chooses Arc as the network and pastes the address. No app to connect.

What does it cost?

There's no Doorstep fee. Each delivery pays its own network fee out of the payment, usually under $0.01 and never more than the limit set in the address's instructions. Any unused part of that allowance goes back to the refund wallet.

What if someone pays too little or too much?

If an address has a minimum or an exact amount, smaller payments wait there until the total is reached; the refund wallet can cancel in the meantime. Anything above the amount is delivered too.

Who holds the money while it's waiting?

Nobody. It sits at the payer's Doorstep address until it's delivered or returned. Doorstep itself holds nothing between transactions.

What if the delivery bot is offline?

Payments wait safely at their address. Anyone can deliver them, including the payer, with one click on the pay page, and the fee comes out of the payment.

Does my contract need changes?

No, as long as it has deposit(uint256 amount, address to) and takes the funds with transferFrom. Every ERC-4626 vault already does. For other functions, put the amount wherever your function expects it.

What if someone sends a token other than USDC?

Doorstep only moves USDC. Other tokens sent to an address can't be delivered or returned by Doorstep, so pay pages say "USDC on the Arc network only".

Is it audited?

Not yet. The contract is about 370 lines, open source, with 32 tests that also run against live mainnet state. An audit is the first thing a grant would pay for.
